newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's forex reserves at $11.82 bln in mid-April.
newsitem.headline: Manila's forex reserves at $11.82 bln in mid-April.

text.p: The Philippines' foreign exchange reserves rose to $11.82 billion as of April 15, up from $11.75 billion at end-1996, the Central Bank said on Sunday.
It said in a statement the reserves remained at a comfortable level, enabling the bank to intervene effectively in the foreign exchange market.

The Central Bank was a net buyer of dollars during the period with total purchases of $1.7 billion, or 13 percent of the total market transactions, and sales of $632 million or 5.0 percent of the total market volume.

The country's net international reserves, or total reserves minus short-term foreign obligations, stood at $10.49 billion, which is $274 million higher than the programmed level of $10.22 billion set under an International Monetary Fund programme, the bank said.
